edits.html:
Rickets: which serum value rises In vitamin D deficiency rickets, alkaline phosphatase activity and PTH (parathyroid hormone) rise, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D falls. Phosphate is low, because less is absorbed and PTH increases its loss in the urine. Calcium is low or normal, because PTH defends it. Osteoblasts make alkaline phosphatase as they lay down bone matrix; it is high in active rickets and often rises before calcium or phosphate falls. PTH raises intestinal calcium absorption only indirectly, by increasing kidney production of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D. In an infant, rickets can present as late crawling or walking with widened wrists.
How NBME framed it The lead-in asked which serum value is increased, and the key was an enzyme activity, alkaline phosphatase, set among minerals (calcium, phosphorus, magnesium) and a liver enzyme. The child was a 15-month-old fed only breast milk who was not yet crawling or walking and had widened wrists.

edits.html:
Class-vs-memberALT activity: ALT (alanine aminotransferase) is a liver enzyme that rises with liver cell injury. When alkaline phosphatase is high and ALT and GGT (gamma-glutamyl transferase) are normal, the source is bone.
Unchecked attributeCalcium concentration: vitamin D deficiency lowers calcium absorption, and PTH (parathyroid hormone) holds serum calcium low or normal. A high calcium points to hyperparathyroidism or vitamin D excess.
Unchecked attributePhosphorus concentration: it falls in vitamin D deficiency, because absorption drops and PTH (parathyroid hormone) increases urinary loss. A high phosphate points to kidney failure or hypoparathyroidism.
True-fact-wrong-slotMagnesium concentration: vitamin D deficiency does not raise it. Magnesium matters to calcium balance in the other direction: a low level impairs PTH (parathyroid hormone) secretion and action.
